messages:
michael: Heads up — I found a SealedSecret in partner-ingest that looks like an old KMS-wrapped blob showing up in our logs. pasted the object id to #incidents earlier. Not sure if it was rewrapped after the last key rotation. tagging @anna-sec for rotation + RBAC review.

anna-sec: thanks for flagging. can you paste the sealedsecret name + small yaml? also any PRs that touched sealed-secrets controller config recently?

michael: here's the snippet I grabbed:
```
kubectl get sealedsecret partner-webhook-secret -n partner-ingest -o yaml
metadata:
  name: partner-webhook-secret
spec:
  encryptedData:
    webhook_key: CiQ...<redacted>
```
no obvious PRs in last 60d that touch the controller SA binding.

samir-devops: i'm oncall, quick thoughts: if it's a wrapped blob using the old crypto key we should rewrap to a temp CMK then reencrypt the SealedSecret, update the controller's grants to the new short-lived key and then revoke legacy grants. play: 1) create temp key redwood-ss-rotate-temp 2) have sealed-secrets controller decrypt & re-encrypt (or run offline rewrap job) 3) rotate/wrap back to production key and revoke old grants. also we need audit backfill to check decrypts from the legacy SA.

michael: plan sounds good. rough commands i'll run:
```bash
# create temporary key (gcp example)
gcloud kms keys create redwood-ss-rotate-temp --location=global --keyring=redwood-rotation --purpose=encryption
# quick rewrap prototype (concept)
python tools/rewrap_sealed_secrets.py --ns partner-ingest --secret partner-webhook-secret --kms-key redwood-ss-rotate-temp
```
I'll open a brief runbook in SEC-1234.

anna-sec: add RBAC steps before we touch production: remove legacy 'legacy-ss-controller' SA from CryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the prod key, create scoped grant for 'ss-controller-canary' with 1h TTL, run rewrap, confirm decrypts in audit logs, then rotate partner SA creds. Also file a partner notification (they need to rotate their webhook signing key if we touch the secret value).

jane-plat: small question — if we rewrap sealed-secrets, will deployed pods pick up new secrets automatically? sealed-secrets controller will reconcile but workloads relying on the secret won't restart by default. suggest: canary restart one deployment (partner-webhook) and watch errors/traces, then proceed to full rollout.

leo-sre: i'll carve a 30m window after your run and stand by for canary restarts. also want to run a search across logs for any plaintext exposure tied to that secret name. opsbot, can you surface decrypt audit counts for the legacy SA in the last 90d?

opsbot: ran query against audit-export. found 14 CryptoKeyVersions.decrypt calls in the last 90 days from serviceAccount:legacy-ss-controller@redwood-project. Link: https://logs.redwood.internal/query?kms_decrypts=14 (internal-only).

michael: good catch. i'll create SEC-1234, include the rewrap script prototype, and schedule the rotation for 2026-03-24T12:30:00Z (12:30 UTC). playbook short: 1) create temp key + grant 2) offline rewrap job -> update SealedSecret objects 3) patch controller to use canary SA -> restart single deployment 4) verify decrypts via audit logs 5) revoke legacy grants + rotate partner creds 6) postmortem snippet.

anna-sec: :thumbsup: no objections. please include exact IAM patch in the runbook and attach the audit query used. ensure ticket has owner and pager assigned. after revoke, run creds-scan and schedule a forced rotation for any rotated partner keys.

jane-plat: i'll handle the canary restart and watch tracing/dashboards. ping me in the thread when the rewrap job finishes.

samir-devops: ack — i'll keep an eye on the rewrap job and stand ready to rollback by restoring the original SealedSecret objects if something fishy happens.

opsbot: opsbot scheduled SEC-1234: rotation run at 2026-03-24T12:30:00Z. Notifying infra-oncall and partner-alerting channel now.

michael: thanks all — i'll post a one-line status update here after the canary completes.
